newsitem.title: CHINA: China premier welcomes Russia PM ahead of deals.
newsitem.headline: China premier welcomes Russia PM ahead of deals.

text.p: Chinese Premier Li Peng on Friday officially welcomed his Russian counterpart Viktor Chernomyrdin to Beijing ahead of talks in which the two are to sign a multi-billion dollar oil and natural gas deal.

Chernomyrdin flew to the Chinese capital on Thursday evening after touring high-tech industries in the southern boomtown of Shenzhen at the start of a three-day visit to China aimed at boosting economic ties between the two neighbours.

Chernomyrdin is scheduled to meet Chinese President Jiang Zemin and is expected to sign a multi-billion dollar oil and natural gas pact with Li after the two hold talks on Friday, diplomats have said.
The agreement would set up the framework for a project to exploit Siberian natural gas to meet China's growing demand for energy, Russian diplomats have said.
The pact would call for cooperation in development of an Irkutsk natural gas field and the construction of a pipeline through Mongolia to energy-short eastern China.
China once was a net oil exporter but its rapid economic growth has fuelled demand for energy.
Chinese officials estimate oil imports could reach an annual 50 million tonnes by the year 2000.
The two leaders are also to sign a railroad agreement that aims to improve rail freight between the two neighbours, the diplomats said.

Chernomyrdin's visit has been preceded by a trip by several economic and energy officials, including First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov and Minister of Foreign Trade Mikhail Fradkov, who have been hammering out details of the deals.

Nemtsov had visited the site of the Three Gorges dam on the Yangtze River and met with senior project officials on Thursday, said an official with the Three Gorges Project Development Co that is overseeing the giant hydroelectric project.
A Russian consortium is bidding for a big contract to supply 14 generators with a total installed capacity of 9,800 megawatts for the hydroelectric power station.

The Three Gorges Development Co official said the firm was still reviewing tenders from several consortia to supply the generating units and had planned to select the winning bidder by late June or early July.
Industry analysts said the Russian group was unlikely to win the contract -- which could be worth some $1 billion -- because of concerns over quality and financing.

Diplomats said Chernomyrdin's visit was aimed chiefly at boosting lagging economic ties with China after a series of high-level official exchanges and presidential summits have bolstered political relations between Moscow and Beijing.
